title: Cube: solved-state end condition in CEL
description:
Express "the cube is solved" as a composable CEL expression.

## Solved state
Each face has all 9 stickers of the same color. The center sticker defines the face color (centers never move).

## CEL expression approach
Need to check 6 faces, each is a 3x3 grid zone. For each zone, all cells have the same component type (color).

### Option A: per-zone check with type_rows
For each zone, type_rows.all(row, row.all(cell, cell == type_rows[0][0]))
But this requires evaluating across 6 zones. Current CEL context only populates lines/rows/cols for the first grid zone.

### Option B: precompute a "solved" boolean per zone
In the CEL context builder, for each grid zone, check if all cells have the same component type. Inject as:
- up_solved, down_solved, front_solved, back_solved, left_solved, right_solved
Then: up_solved && down_solved && front_solved && back_solved && left_solved && right_solved

### Option C: multi-zone CEL context
Extend the CEL context builder to populate lines/rows for ALL grid zones (keyed by zone name):
- zones.up.type_rows, zones.front.type_rows, etc.
Then: ["up","down","front","back","left","right"].all(face, zones[face].solved)

## Recommendation
Option B is simplest and works within current architecture. Option C is more general but requires refactoring the CEL context builder.

## Dependencies
- May require extending CEL context to support multiple grid zones
- Current populate_grid_lines() breaks after first grid zone — needs to handle all zones

## Test
Set up a solved cube state, evaluate the end condition CEL expression, verify true. Rotate one face, verify false.
